summary.intent: Implement SDK-based E2E and load tests for CipherBox as two new workspace packages, replacing browser-automation Playwright tests with direct SDK calls for faster, more reliable testing.
summary.outcome: Created tests/sdk-e2e (83 tests across 10 suites, all passing) and tests/load (5 scenarios with metrics infrastructure), plus a throttle bypass mechanism, CI workflows, and resolved a batch of PR review comments.

repo: ThrottlerGuard is applied per-controller via @UseGuards(), not globally — requires touching ~7 controllers to swap the guard implementation
Individual @Throttle() decorators on specific endpoints (e.g., IPNS publish: 10/min) are separate from the controller-level ThrottlerGuard and need independent bypass handling
setApiClientConfig is a module-level singleton because orval generates standalone functions (not class methods) that import customInstance directly — there is no object to hold instance state
NODE_ENV in apps/api/.env overrides shell environment variables passed to nest start --watch, because ConfigModule.forRoot() loads .env and wins
The /auth/test-login endpoint has its own strict @Throttle (5 per 15 min) separate from the general controller throttle
pnpm workspace lockfile is updated automatically when running pnpm install from the root — new packages don't require a separate lockfile update step
release-please-config.json has an extra-files list for package.json files to keep versions in sync across non-standard packages
Playwright's webServer config in playwright.config.ts handles starting the API for E2E tests — the API is not started separately in e2e.yml

code.finding: Gold standard pattern for SDK test setup: test-login → initializeVault → encryptVaultKeys → setApiClientConfig → new CipherBoxClient → registerFolder. All SDK E2E tests derive from this pattern.
Module-level _config singleton with getCachedInstance() — extended to support optional defaultHeaders for injecting bypass/auth headers into all axios requests without per-call changes
ThrottlerModule configured with limit:10/ttl:1000 (10 req/s) and limit:100/ttl:60000 (100 req/min) — these are per-IP by default, not per-user

Custom BypassableThrottlerGuard uses process.env directly (not ConfigService) and timingSafeEqual for constant-time comparison — skips throttle when X-Throttle-Bypass header matches THROTTLE_BYPASS_SECRET
crypto.getRandomValues() has a hard 65536 byte limit per call — files >64KB require chunked generation in a loop

The setApiClientConfig singleton gets overwritten by multi-account test fixtures (share/invite suites) — requires re-setting the config at the start of any test suite that runs after multi-account tests

workflow: 1Password SSH agent for commit signing is not accessible from Claude agent subprocesses — commits must be retried or run from the user's terminal
sed-based bulk replacements on TypeScript files are unreliable for nested delimiters (parentheses) — prefer targeted Edit tool calls or full file rewrites
Running tsc --noEmit for type checking requires dependencies to be built first (e.g., api-client must be rebuilt before sdk-e2e can typecheck against it)
When using Promise.allSettled in load test scenarios, errors inside workload functions are silently swallowed unless rejection reasons are explicitly logged
pnpm --filter <package> dev for NestJS does hot-reload — changes to app.module.ts take effect without restart, but only after the process detects file changes

friction: 1Password SSH agent timed out mid-session, causing multiple commit failures that required retries or user intervention
MODULE-LEVEL SINGLETON: setApiClientConfig being global caused cross-suite test contamination — required a re-set workaround in error-cases.test.ts and a switchTo() hack in multi-account fixture
NODE_ENV=test passed via shell was silently overridden by NODE_ENV=development in apps/api/.env — wasted time before discovering ConfigModule loads .env with higher precedence
crypto.getRandomValues() 65536 byte limit caused silent crashes in the upload workload (error swallowed by Promise.allSettled) — hard to diagnose without explicit rejection logging
sed bulk-replace of header patterns corrupted vault-lifecycle.test.ts by adding unmatched parentheses — required a full file rewrite to recover
The rate limiter blocked all tests before the bypass was implemented, making it impossible to run more than ~1 test suite before hitting 429
The per-endpoint @Throttle decorators (especially IPNS publish at 10/min) are still causing 429s in load tests even with the bypass guard — root cause not yet confirmed
open_items: Refactor api-client from module-level singleton to instance-scoped axios: configure orval to generate functions accepting an axios instance, thread through sdk-core's SdkContext, have CipherBoxClient own its axios instance — tracked in .planning/todos/pending/2026-03-22-refactor-api-client-from-singleton-to-instance-scoped-axios.md

Investigate @Throttle decorator bypass gap: verify whether BypassableThrottlerGuard's canActivate override is reached for per-endpoint @Throttle decorators, or whether 429s come from upstream IPFS — tracked in .planning/todos/pending/2026-03-22-investigate-throttle-bypass-gap-for-per-endpoint-throttle-decorators.md

Migrate raw fetch() calls in vault-lifecycle, share-operations, and invite-link test suites to use the orval-generated API client functions — would eliminate testFetch() helper and automatically propagate defaultHeaders
PR review comments batch (24 threads) — fixes were implemented and committed but replies/resolutions to threads were in progress when the transcript ended
Load test 429 errors mean reported throughput numbers are unreliable until the IPNS publish throttle bypass is confirmed working — baseline metrics from the local stack run are provisional
